unlock_procedure: 1. An operator with push rights on Extr3sao/bot_crypto creates a token (PAT with repo scope) or, preferably, installs and signs in the gh CLI.
2. Export it only for the shell that pushes: export GITHUB_TOKEN=<token> (never in a file inside the repo, never in a commit).
3. Verify it is not already leaked: git config --get credential.helper must NOT contain the token, and the token must not appear in any tracked file.

4. Push the WP branch without storing the credential: GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git -c credential.helper='!f() { echo username=x-access-token; echo password=$GITHUB_TOKEN; }; f' push --set-upstream origin HEAD:refs/heads/agent/edge-recovery/WP-EDGE-02
5. Alternative without env vars: gh auth login (https or ssh) and then git push --set-upstream origin HEAD:refs/heads/agent/edge-recovery/WP-EDGE-02.

6. Alternative through the interactive helper: run git push once from an interactive terminal so the manager stores the credential in the OS keychain, then the dry-run above must return 'Everything up-to-date'.
7. Confirm from a clean session: GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git ls-remote --heads origin 'refs/heads/agent/edge-recovery/*' must now list the pushed branch and its sha.
8. Record the resulting sha in this report (push.published_sha) and re-run scripts/edge01_wp02_verify.py to confirm the artefacts are the committed ones.
9. If the operator prefers, the same branch can be pushed over SSH after adding a key: git remote set-url --push origin git@github.com:Extr3sao/bot_crypto.git.
